questions.ask: What is your date of birth?
What are the last four digits of the phone number on file?

hints.day_month_swapped: Could you say the month as a word, please?

intents.hardship: The customer mentions illness, a death in the family or job loss.
intents.dispute: "This debt is not mine" or "I never had this product"; a claim that the product was closed or paid off in the past is also a dispute.
intents.already_paid: "I already paid": only a payment of this past-due amount.
intents.restructure: A request for a new payment plan or lower instalments.
intents.vague: A vague period such as "next week", "end of the month" or "when my salary comes".
intents.too_much: The customer says the full amount is too much.

lines.ask_today: Can you make this payment today?
lines.ask_today_multi: Can you make these payments today?
lines.next_product: Now let's look at the next product.

lines.offer_floor: I understand. Could you pay {amount}? The rest stays overdue.

lines.below_floor_again: I'm sorry, I can't record that amount.

rules.skipped_repeat_counts.assumption: The brief only says "Do not repeat an offer the customer already refused." and never says whether a skipped step uses an attempt; the engine default applies. With this ladder no step can equal an earlier one (attempt 1 is never today; attempt 2 is the floor on the deadline).

quotes: A no to paying today with no date and no amount is a flat refusal.
A flat refusal or a non-answer uses one persuasion attempt.
Attempt 1: propose the last business day of this week.
rules.opening_is_attempt.derivation: Refusing the opening ask (pay today) is a flat refusal that leads to attempt 1, the end-of-week proposal. The opening is therefore not attempt 1, and the band counts (1 and 2) are the proposals after the opening.

rules.opening_blocks_repeat.assumption: The brief does not say whether the opening ask counts as a proposal for the no-repeat rule. No ladder step can equal it (attempt 1 moves to next week when today is the last business day of the week), so the default false applies.

rules.too_much_skips_full.assumption: The brief does not say this; after 'too much', attempt 1 uses full_or_floor, so the floor is proposed.

quotes: If the customer says the full amount is too much, offer the floor, once.
Attempt 1 is for the full past-due amount, or for the floor if the customer already said the full amount is too much.
Attempt 2 may name the floor again, on the deadline.
rules.too_much_floor.derivation: The floor is offered once after 'too much', and that offer is attempt 1 (on attempt 1's date). Attempt 2 names the floor 'again' on the deadline. An extra floor offer on the asked date that uses no attempt would name the floor before attempt 1 as well, breaking 'once'.

rules.ladder_repeat_last.assumption: There is no repeat of the last step. When attempts are used up, the agent stops (rule 31).

quotes: A flat refusal or a non-answer uses one persuasion attempt.
If the customer refuses the deadline, treat it as a flat refusal (rule 30).
If it fails, try once more.
Offer to connect them with the customer support team.
A promise date must be today or later, a business day, and not after the deadline.
rules.deadline_adjust.derivation: Deadlines are counted in business days, so they are already business days. previous_business_day keeps any moved date within the deadline.

quotes: Ask for the full past-due amount first.
Can you make this payment today?
Attempt 1: propose the last business day of this week. If today is that day, propose the last business day of next week.

products.floor_pct.assumption: The floor is a field, not a percentage: minimum_payment or instalment_amount.

products.floor_full_below.assumption: No threshold below which the full debt is the floor.

products.floor_round.assumption: There is no rounding because the floor is read from the account.

products.step_round.assumption: There are no percentage ladder steps.

products.promise_scale.assumption: create_promise takes the same unit as get_account.

multi.outcome_priority.assumption: Brief A covers one product, so the first product's ending is used.

multi.order.assumption: Brief A covers one product, so the account order is used.

event_changes.assumption: There are no dated code changes.

changes.assumption: There are no dated value changes.

assumptions: The brief names no currency, so the default 'dollars' is used.
max_unclear is not set: the brief has no separate count for unclear answers to payment questions. A non-answer uses a persuasion attempt (rule 30), so non_answer_counts is true.
callback.business_days_only is false: 'today' is allowed as stated, and only the second day must be the next business day.
date_order is dmy, per 'Read a date given only as numbers as day, then month, then year.' Example: '05/03/1980' is sent as 1980-03-05.
The verify response fields come from the API: ok, verified (boolean), all_verified, wrong_answers_left, hint. An unreadable answer returns ok=false and is not counted as wrong.
Floor names: 'minimum payment' for credit cards and 'instalment' for loans, based on the field names minimum_payment and instalment_amount.
Attempt counts are copied as stated: early 1, late 2. They are counted after the opening ask, whose refusal uses one attempt and leads to attempt 1.

Ladder step 1 is full_or_floor on the last business day of this week, or of next week when today is that day (rule 30). Step 2 (late band only) is the floor on the deadline. Example: today Friday 2026-10-16, late band: attempt 1 is Friday 2026-10-23; the deadline is the 7th business day after today, skipping the 2026-10-26 holiday, which is 2026-10-28.
too_much_floor is asked_date: the floor offer after 'too much' is for the date on the table and uses no attempt. Its refusal is a flat refusal that uses an attempt (rules 26 and 30).
Rule 22 ('next Friday' means the Friday of the following calendar week) maps to next_weekday 'following_week'.
Rule 1 requires telling the caller that the call is recorded; the opening says 'We record this call'.
Brief A never uses add_note, so notes are disabled and every event note is empty.
The human transfer uses queue 'general' (rule 42); restructuring and support use their own queues.
'If a transfer follows a recorded promise, close as transferred with that transfer's reason' is handled by the built-in rule that a transfer ends the call with the transfer event.
The only rule on changing a recorded promise is the mobile app (rule 36), which is used in promise_change.
Rule 45 (two 'I don't want to talk' replies) maps to max_not_talk 2: before verification the call closes as not_verified/declined, after it as no_promise/refused.
